items.title: ABA Law Library Collection Periodicals
items.description: Every current and historical ABA periodical, including 44 titles normally locked to section members.

items.title: Academic OneFile
items.description: Eight thousand peer-reviewed journals plus newspapers and reference works. Good for the non-law half of an interdisciplinary paper.

items.title: Academic Search Complete
items.description: The general scholarly database. Reach for it when your topic runs past law into medicine, education or social policy.

items.title: Academic Video Online
items.description: Sixty-seven thousand films and documentaries. Occasionally the fastest way to understand an unfamiliar industry.

items.title: Bar Journals
items.description: Roughly 160 state and city bar journals. Practitioners write here about problems before the law reviews notice them.

items.title: Boston Business Journal
items.description: Local business news, useful for tracking the companies your summer employer works with. You set up the login yourself.

items.title: Boston Globe
items.description: Three ways in: as a secondary source inside Westlaw or Lexis+, through the Sawyer guide, or in print at the library going back two months.

items.title: CALI Lessons
items.description: Hundreds of interactive lessons across 40-plus subjects, covering every 1L course, with real-time feedback. Get the authorization code from the research desk.

items.title: Caselaw Access Project
items.description: Six and a half million decisions from every state, federal and territorial court, free and open. No login, no seat limit.

items.title: Checkpoint Edge
items.description: RIA's tax research service, covering federal, state, international and IFRS, plus Catalyst for comparative tax planning.

items.title: Chronicle of Higher Education
items.description: Higher education news and data back to 1989. The standard source for education law work.

items.title: CLBB NeuroLaw Library
items.description: Curated neuroscience-and-law scholarship, amicus briefs and affidavits, free to anyone. Niche, but nothing else collects it.

items.title: Code of Federal Regulations
items.description: The official codified text of federal agency regulations. Start here rather than a vendor's copy when the exact wording matters.

items.title: Compilation of Presidential Documents
items.description: Everything the White House Press Secretary releases, officially published. Proclamations, executive orders, remarks.

items.title: Congress.gov
items.description: The official record of federal legislation. Bill text, status, sponsors, committee reports, and the Congressional Record.

items.title: CourtLink
items.description: Federal and state dockets and filed documents inside Lexis. This is what you use instead of PACER, which the library does not provide.

items.title: CourtListener
items.description: Three million opinions, free, plus the RECAP archive of PACER documents other people have already paid for.

items.title: Criminal Justice Abstracts
items.description: Scholarship on criminology, corrections, policing and criminal procedure. The empirical literature behind the doctrine.

items.title: Current Index to Legal Periodicals
items.description: A weekly index of new law review articles, published by the University of Washington for close to ninety years. Good for a literature check before you commit to a note topic.

items.title: Decisis
items.description: A citator and research platform, free to Massachusetts Bar Association members. Student MBA membership gets you in.

items.title: EBSCOHost
items.description: The EBSCO platform itself, searching up to 53 databases at once. Broad, and blunt.

items.title: Educational Resource Information Center
items.description: Education research, curriculum materials, dissertations and conference papers. The evidence base for education law arguments.

items.title: Elgaronline
items.description: Edward Elgar's ebooks and research handbooks, weighted toward international and comparative law.

items.title: English Reports
items.description: Page images of the original English Reports, the Statutes of the Realm from 1235, and pre-1865 law reports. For legal history and for common-law origin questions.

items.title: Environmental Law Reporter
items.description: Monthly analysis of environmental law and policy, written for practitioners rather than academics.

items.title: Federal Register
items.description: The daily journal of the federal government, carrying proposed rules, final rules and notices. Where a regulation lives before it reaches the CFR.

items.title: Foreign Law Guide
items.description: How to find the law of about 190 jurisdictions, with citations to primary sources. Start here before you start guessing.

items.title: General Court of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
items.description: Massachusetts statutes, session laws and bill history, straight from the legislature.

items.title: Google Scholar
items.description: Free and broad. Turn on library links in preferences so results route through Suffolk's subscriptions.

items.title: GovInfo
items.description: The GPO's own archive of federal regulations, presidential documents, court opinions and congressional material. Authenticated and citable.

items.title: GreenFILE
items.description: Scholarship on human impact on the environment, spanning law, science and policy.

items.title: HeinOnline
items.description: Nearly 200 million pages of law reviews, government documents and historical material. Suffolk licenses twelve collections. The best archive of legal scholarship anywhere.

items.title: Index to Foreign Legal Periodicals
items.description: A subject index to international and comparative law journals and essay collections.

items.title: Index to Legal Periodicals (1981-present)
items.description: Indexes legal periodicals and books from 1981 forward. Use it alongside HeinOnline when you need coverage rather than full text.

items.title: Index to Legal Periodicals Retrospective: 1908-1981
items.description: Indexes over 750 legal periodicals from 1908 to 1981. The only practical way into pre-1981 scholarship by subject.

items.title: Indian Claims Insight
items.description: Court documents, treaties, congressional publications and maps covering the Indian Claims Commission and its history.

items.title: Indigenous Peoples of the Americas: History, Culture & Law
items.description: Treaties, federal statutes and regulations, case law, tribal codes and constitutions, plus rare historical material.

items.title: Inside Higher Ed
items.description: Daily news and analysis on higher education. Pairs with the Chronicle.

items.title: Intellectual Property Law Collection
items.description: Legislative histories, treatises and periodicals on copyright, patent and trademark, plus FCC material.

items.title: Investor-State Law Guide
items.description: Rules, conventions, bilateral investment treaties and awards for investment treaty arbitration, which is an expensive subscription anywhere else.

items.title: Journal of the American Medical Association
items.description: JAMA in full, for health law work that turns on clinical evidence.

items.title: JSTOR
items.description: Academic journals, books and primary sources across every discipline, with deep back-runs.

items.title: Kanopy
items.description: Streaming documentaries and films. Access is limited and faculty course requests take priority.

items.title: Law Journal Collection
items.description: Over 3,400 scholarly journals from first issue to current. Broad multidisciplinary coverage.

items.title: Law360
items.description: Daily legal news across eleven bureaus. Also reachable free inside your Lexis account under News.

items.title: LawArXiv
items.description: Open access preprints of legal scholarship, run by law librarians and scholars. Where articles appear before publication.

items.title: Legislative Insight
items.description: Compiled federal legislative histories with the underlying documents attached. Saves days of reconstruction work.

items.title: Lexis+
items.description: One of the two major research platforms, and where Lexis+ AI (Protege) and Practical Guidance live. Register with your Suffolk address.

items.title: LGBTQ+ Rights
items.description: Subject-coded materials tracing the gay rights movement in America and the law that came out of it.

items.title: Library Catalog
items.description: The law library's own catalog. Search here for course reserves, print study aids and anything physical.

items.title: LLMC Digital
items.description: A large archive of historical legal documents from around the world, including material long out of print.

items.title: Massachusetts Criminal Practice
items.description: A research aid on Massachusetts criminal law. Check the publication date on individual chapters before relying on them.

items.title: Massachusetts Docket Search
items.description: Basic case information and scheduled court dates from the Massachusetts trial courts, free to the public.

items.title: Massachusetts Lawyers Weekly
items.description: Appellate and trial court decisions, verdicts and settlements, and court rule changes. Paywalled to everyone else.

items.title: Massachusetts Prosecutor's Guide
items.description: Judge Stearns' full-text guide to Massachusetts criminal practice, updated through the year and linked to masscases.com.

items.title: Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court: Oral Arguments
items.description: Recorded oral arguments from the SJC. Listen to one before you moot.

items.title: Massachusetts Trial Court Law Libraries
items.description: The best free starting point for Massachusetts research, with subject guides written by court librarians.

items.title: MCLE OnlinePass
items.description: MCLE's practice manuals, over 400 ebooks, streaming CLE, and Massachusetts agency decisions. Practicing attorneys pay real money for this.

items.title: MEDLINE
items.description: The medical literature. Health law and any case turning on standard of care.

items.title: NAACP Papers
items.description: NAACP records, federal government files and personal papers documenting the twentieth-century Black freedom struggle.

items.title: National Indian Law Library
items.description: The Native American Rights Fund's library, devoted to federal Indian and tribal law. Free.

items.title: New York Times
items.description: Full digital access, free with your Suffolk email. Re-register every year or it lapses quietly.

items.title: OECD Library
items.description: OECD books, papers, statistics and indicators. Comparative economic and regulatory data.

items.title: Oxford English Dictionary
items.description: Historical meanings with dated citations. Reach for it when a statute turns on what a word meant when it was enacted.

items.title: Oxford Journals Online
items.description: Three hundred journals from Oxford University Press across law and the social sciences.

items.title: Oxford Scholarship Online: Law Collection
items.description: Oxford's legal monographs in full text. Book-length treatment when an article is not enough.

items.title: PACER
items.description: Federal court records, priced per page. The library does not cover it, so use CourtLink or the RECAP archive first.

items.title: Past Faculty Exams
items.description: Real exams from Suffolk professors, searchable, and not the same set as what sits on Canvas. Ask your professor first about theirs.

items.title: Practical Law
items.description: Checklists, standard documents and practice notes inside Westlaw. How a transaction is actually done, rather than the theory.

items.title: Project Syndicate
items.description: Commentary from economists, policymakers and scholars. Useful for framing a policy argument.

items.title: ProView
items.description: Thomson Reuters treatises as ebooks, searchable by title, subject and jurisdiction.

items.title: PsycArticles
items.description: Full-text psychology scholarship from the APA. Relevant to competency, eyewitness and juvenile work.

items.title: PsycINFO
items.description: The largest index of behavioral science and mental health literature.

items.title: Regulations.gov
items.description: Track federal rulemaking and read the public comments. Where you find out who opposed a rule and why.

items.title: Regulatory Insight
items.description: Compiled regulatory histories, tracing a rule from proposal to final text.

items.title: SCOTUSblog
items.description: Supreme Court coverage before argument, after argument, and after decision. Free, and better than the news.

items.title: Social Law Library
items.description: Massachusetts administrative decisions from the ABCC, Appellate Tax Board, DEP, DIA, DLR, MCAD and the Ethics Commission. Often the only place they exist.

items.title: SSRN
items.description: Working papers and preprints across law and the social sciences. Where scholarship appears first.

items.title: State House News Service
items.description: Wire coverage of Massachusetts state government, filed daily. Normally institutional-only.

items.title: Statistical Abstract of the United States
items.description: Social, political and economic statistics from 1878 forward. A fast way to source a number.

items.title: Statistical Insight
items.description: Indexed statistics from federal, state, private and international sources, with the underlying tables.

items.title: Supreme Court Insight
items.description: Supreme Court dockets, briefs, joint appendices and oral argument transcripts back to 1955.

items.title: Taylor & Francis Journal Database
items.description: Peer-reviewed articles across the Taylor and Francis, Routledge and Dove Medical imprints.

items.title: Transnational Dispute Management
items.description: A peer-reviewed journal on international arbitration, weighted toward investment arbitration.

items.title: Trends and Policy
items.description: Timelines of federal law and policy by subject, showing how a regime developed.

items.title: U.K. Parliamentary Papers
items.description: British parliamentary material, including select committee reports and command papers. For comparative and historical work.

items.title: U.S. Congressional Documents
items.description: The bound Congressional Record and its predecessor titles, plus the daily edition back to 1980.

items.title: U.S. Federal Legislative and Executive Materials
items.description: Congressional documents from 1789 to the present, in one collection.

items.title: United Nations Treaty Collection
items.description: Full text of international treaties, including everything deposited with the Secretary-General, and each country's ratification status.

items.title: United States Code
items.description: The official codification of federal statutes by subject. Cite this rather than a vendor's version.

items.title: Wall Street Journal
items.description: Full text, free. Sign up at Suffolk's own URL rather than the public one.

items.title: Washington Post
items.description: Free through Suffolk with your own account.

items.title: West Academic Assessment
items.description: Multiple choice, short answer and essay questions keyed to your actual casebook, with sample answers and commentary. Separate from the study aid library and easy to miss.

items.title: West Academic Study Aids
items.description: The whole subscription library: Nutshells, Hornbooks, Examples and Explanations, Black Letter Outlines, Gilbert, Exam Pro, plus audiobooks and recorded lectures. Suffolk's entire commercial study aid spend is here.

items.title: Westlaw Advantage
items.description: The other major platform, and where CoCounsel and Practical Law live. Register with your Suffolk address.

items.title: Westlaw Campus Research
items.description: A lighter Westlaw for alumni and anyone without an active academic account.

items.title: Wiley Online Library
items.description: Journals, reference works and ebooks. Suffolk's subscription does not cover everything you will see listed.

items.title: WIPO Lex
items.description: National IP statutes, treaties and WIPO-administered instruments from around the world.

items.title: World Constitutions Illustrated: Contemporary & Historical Documents and Resources
items.description: Every country's current constitution in the original language with an English translation, plus substantial constitutional history.

items.title: WorldCat
items.description: Finds which library holds a physical item. Pair it with interlibrary loan when Suffolk does not have the book.

items.title: WorldTradeLaw.net
items.description: Trade news and a subscription service summarising every WTO dispute settlement decision.

descriptions: written for LITSA; vendor copy discarded
